event: Reported FCC approval for an initial batch of about 500 wire centers, about 10 percent of AT&T's footprint, set to take effect in June 2026.
Customers in wire centers in 18 states told that copper landline service could be discontinued starting November 15, 2026.
Applies to the FCC to discontinue copper landline service in wire centers serving about 90,000 customers in 18 states.
AT&T's 18-state application granted automatically, 31 days after public notice.
Closes its acquisition of Frontier.

Adopts FCC 26-19 (released March 27): network change disclosure filings eliminated, 31-day automatic grant for discontinuance applications, blanket grandfathering, preemption of conflicting state and local rules.
Reports 15.0 million retail switched access lines at June 30, 2025, down from 18.2 million a year earlier; 8.6 million are business lines.
Files to discontinue legacy voice in portions of 360 California wire centers, about 184,000 residential and 15,000 business customers, proposed on or after June 1, 2027.
FCC grants AT&T's California discontinuance, about 184,000 locations, with service continuing until on or after June 1, 2027. AT&T's request to preempt California rules is still pending.
Files for portions of eight states (about 140,000 legacy voice lines in use), plus a companion application for about 16,500 business lines.
Stops service in another batch of areas the FCC had allowed it to discontinue after network damage.
Files for nine states: AZ, DE, NJ, NM, OH, RI, SC, UT, VA.
Public notice DA 26-861 sets AT&T business-line (AL, AR, GA, LA, SC, TN) and residential (AL, LA, MS) applications for automatic grant on September 14, 2026.
Bulletin reports 494 AT&T copper retirement notices in 2025, a 21-state AT&T discontinued-service workbook and Lumen's 2025 close of new copper POTS orders.
Verizon's eight-state application granted automatically.
Has approval to discontinue legacy services at more than 30 percent of its roughly 4,600 copper wire centers and to stop new sales at more than 85 percent.
Asks the FCC for authority not to restore service in more than 600 areas across 16 states where copper was damaged.
Applies to discontinue legacy service in parts of eight states, from September through November 2026.
Public notice DA 26-890 sets the nine-state request for automatic grant on September 26, 2026, discontinuance proposed on or after October 23, 2026.

Files for portions of California, Connecticut, D.C., Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, New York, Pennsylvania and West Virginia, where about 750,000 locations still use legacy voice; proposed on or after November 30, 2026.
Nine-state request removed from automatic grant; not a final determination.
More AT&T discontinuance applications set for automatic approval on October 5, October 18, October 22 and November 20, 2026.

Public notice DA 26-1075: AT&T CLEC business landline service (PrimePath and Business Local Exchange Service) in 34 states and D.C., deemed granted November 5, 2026 absent FCC action (WC Docket 26-276).
Files comments urging the FCC to pause the AT&T business-line application under DA 26-1075.
